clue.text: No common clay, this element

parts.note: something that is not common is rare
clay is a kind of earth or soil

explanation.surface: A scientist remarks that this element is no ordinary clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gave 'clement'; the page prints 'element'. Rare earths are the lanthanide metals, so the two halves of the wordplay double as a sly description.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths are a family of metallic elements, so one of them is an element.

clue.text: Arcane sort of cheer about what is dear in France

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the French word
a sort of cheer is a jumbled version of the word

parts.note: cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: An obscure kind of cheer for something precious in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges CHEER as RE...CHE, and 'about' wraps that round CHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recherche is rare and far-fetched, recondite and known to few.

clue.text: Nurse treated such old characters

indicators.note: treated means worked on or processed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse looks after some elderly eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like odd people; it means letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the letters of the ancient Germanic alphabet, written characters of old.

clue.text: Sweep-shots in which England's opening pair failed badly

parts.note: the first two letters of the word England

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of failed are disordered

explanation.surface: Cricket: England's openers flop against sweep shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, with sweep shots and an opening pair; the definition is military fire raking a line of troops end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfilade is gunfire sweeping along a line of troops from one end.

clue.text: To go into the country, trick is to make interior rail-change

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

indicators.note: change signals that the letters of rail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway plan to switch track inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns RAIL into RALI, and 'interior' places it inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make rustic or move to a farming life is to go off to the countryside.

clue.text: Using camouflage, I have row in Dad's Army

indicators.note: the letters go inside the Home Guard abbreviation

parts.note: Dad's Army was the nickname of the Home Guard, HG
a din is a row, a racket

explanation.surface: An old soldier in the Home Guard hides while quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is the nickname of Britain's wartime Home Guard (HG), and a TV sitcom about it. 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Camouflage is a way of concealing yourself from view.

clue.text: Watery-eyed listener to lawman

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Law, a man of law
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone tearful lends an ear to a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear describes eyes dimmed and watery, as with tears or tiredness.

clue.text: This sea-area is cold in sound

indicators.note: the letters go inside the word for sound

parts.note: a sound is an inlet, like a bay

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster says this sea zone sounds chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: Biscay is a sea area in the BBC Shipping Forecast. 'sound' is not noise but an inlet of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Biscay names one of the zones of the maritime weather forecast.

clue.text: Sort of roll (A-E, etc)

indicators.note: sort of signals a jumble of the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters A and E
the letters etc as written

explanation.surface: A list sorted alphabetically, from A to E and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: The voters' list is printed in alphabetical order, from A-E onwards, so the whole clue is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The register of voters is arranged alphabetically, a roll of names A to Z.

clue.text: Moving arm up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same both up and down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An arm moving up and down like a pump handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The down entry reads the same both up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning blade on a helicopter or in a motor is a revolving part.

clue.text: Does this carry gale warnings too?

definitions.text: Does this carry gale warnings too?

parts.words: Does this carry gale warnings too?
parts.note: storm warnings were once shown by hoisting cones on coastal masts, and this tree also bears cones

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what displays storm signals.
explanation.walkthrough: British coastguards hoisted black canvas cones as gale warnings; a pine or fir carries cones of its own, hence 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-bearing tree is defined by the cones it carries, the same shape as the old storm signal.

clue.text: Coming down, was Camptown jockey put off it?

definitions.text: was Camptown jockey put off it?

explanation.surface: A rider at the Camptown races tumbles from the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Camptown Races is an American folk song about horse racing. The second half reads the word as a jockey's fall from the horse, or as DE-SCENT, being put off the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down is a falling or dismounting, and a jockey thrown off the horse makes that downward drop.

clue.text: Rest left to the end for support

indicators.note: says the left letter is attached after the word for rest

parts.note: to rest is to ease off

explanation.surface: Something left at the back to lean against.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holds up a canvas, so it is a support.

clue.text: Time-honour'd aircraft?

explanation.surface: An old aeroplane praised for its long service.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard II opens with 'Old John of Gaunt, time-honour'd Lancaster'; the Avro Lancaster was a Second World War British bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's epithet for John of Gaunt, Duke of that house, and the name of a famous wartime bomber plane.

clue.text: Eg slack row inspired by miners

explanation.surface: Some idle argument stirred up by pit workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Slack is the fine small coal left after screening. A dust is old slang for a row, as in dust-up; the dust miners breathe in is from coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack is powdered small coal, and the fine particles colliers inhale underground are the same powder.

clue.text: Prominent Greek feature line in a Scorpio, perhaps

indicators.note: the line letter goes into the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests a possible variant of a Scorpio's letters

explanation.surface: Astrology: a line in a Scorpio's horoscope shows a Greek trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A SCORPIO, and 'in' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The citadel above Athens is the most famous landmark of Greece.

clue.text: How to deal with present strike by women

parts.note: to strike is to rap or knock

explanation.surface: Advice on handling the current industrial stoppage by women workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like the time now, but it is a gift; 'strike' is not a walk-out but a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is covered in paper before it is given, which is the way to handle it.

clue.text: Pair admitting Hieland trick in court

indicators.note: the pair letters take the rearranged letters inside
trick signals the letters of Hieland are played about with

explanation.surface: A couple accept a Highland trick in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: Hieland is Scots for Highland. 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or woo casually, as a suitor pays court.

clue.text: Food in cans?

parts.note: can is slang for prison, and a prison sentence is called by the name of a breakfast oatmeal

explanation.surface: A question about tinned food.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang 'doing porridge' means serving a jail term; 'the can' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal gruel is a food, and British slang for a jail term, time spent in the can.

clue.text: Like a good monk, taking to Bede in translation

indicators.note: translation renders the words in another form, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A monk translating the Venerable Bede is well behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: Bede was an English monk and historian; monks take a vow of obedience.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks vow obedience, so a good one is dutiful and compliant.

clue.text: Gain by Labour

parts.note: reads like a political party's success, but means getting money through work

explanation.surface: The Labour Party makes ground at an election.
explanation.definitionFit: To be paid in return for work is to acquire money through toil.

clue.text: Spots the trouble — mainly pathological, not well internally

indicators.note: says the word for not well goes inside the shortened word
most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: pathological can mean morbid, unhealthy
someone not well is ill

explanation.surface: A doctor diagnoses a rash as largely disease-driven and unhealthy within.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray '1'. 'mainly' trims MORBID to MORBI, and 'internally' puts ILL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical name for measles, the illness marked by red spots.

clue.text: Be economical with pickle

explanation.surface: A thrifty way of preserving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' is not preserving but a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to save money, and a fix or jam is an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Chemistry in schools has a bad reputation

explanation.surface: School chemistry is held in low regard.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public-school slang chemistry lessons were nicknamed for their smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school slang for the science of smelly experiments, and a verb meaning is badly regarded.

clue.text: Short measure alternative condenser

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: capacity is a measure of volume
OR introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Giving short measure is presented as another kind of condensing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts CAPACITY to CAPACIT. Condenser is the older name for this electrical component.
explanation.definitionFit: Condenser was the older term for the component that stores electric charge between plates.

clue.text: Long for county check

parts.note: to vet is to check

explanation.surface: Eager to inspect the shire.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn to possess something is to desire it enviously.

clue.text: Rejected a benefit for the huntress

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a can be written an
a benefit is an aid

explanation.surface: Someone turned down for a state handout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns AN AID round to make the Roman goddess of the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting and the moon.

clue.text: Sailors' stop in Java Strait

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found within Java Strait

explanation.surface: Sailors halt in an Indonesian sea passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avast' is the nautical command to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a seaman's order to cease or hold.

clue.text: Most booed player of football team at home

parts.note: Villa is Aston Villa, a Birmingham football club
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A footballer is jeered when his side plays at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club in Birmingham. 'Player' is an actor: the villain is the one the panto audience boos.
explanation.definitionFit: In a melodrama or pantomime the audience hisses the wicked character above all others.

clue.text: Decline grievous to the reactionary

parts.note: to die is to fade or decline
grievous means hard to bear

explanation.surface: A painful slump hits a conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn conservative who resists all change is a reactionary.

clue.text: Eat small amount — it makes sense

explanation.surface: Have a little bite, a sensible idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a bit of it, and the sense on the tongue is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Addison's organ not the subject of disease?

explanation.surface: Addison's body part was free of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison co-founded the 18th-century periodical of this name. 'Addison's disease' is a real illness, the misdirection; an onlooker watches rather than suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodical Addison ran, and an onlooker who watches rather than being the patient.
